paragraphs: So it is cited in the Arukh, entry לך; Hyman identifies him as Rabbi Abba bar Yaakov, as in Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit, chapter 1, halakhah 6.[^1]

notes.text: The actual Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 1:6 paragraph explicitly has Rabbi Abba bar Yaakov in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, locally supporting that title and the contextual ב"י expansion. Hyman’s Rabbah-to-Abba identification and report of the Arukh entry לך remain his claims; that Arukh entry was not freshly collated. No identity merge or legal teaching is imported.
